entities.summary:
François de Chevert (1695–1769) was a French general of the eighteenth century who rose by merit through the royal army, celebrated for bravery at Prague (1741) during the War of the Austrian Succession and for steady service under Louis XV. Of relatively modest origin compared with court grandees, he became a symbol of professional officership rewarded by the monarchy.

Chevert’s reputation rested on disciplined infantry leadership in the complex coalition wars that followed the Polish and Austrian succession crises. Memoir and popular anecdote later embellished his courage, making him a didactic hero of Napoleonic-era readers looking back to Bourbon martial virtue.

Military historians place him among the competent Louis Quinze commanders who sustained French operational skill even as strategic outcomes varied.
